title: Weekend capacity quiet-mode briefing notes (personal scratch)
content:
Context: quick personal scratchpad for the weekend quiet-mode plan. Not for direct copy->send yet. I want to capture the framing, short scripts, likely Qs, and the absolute must-haves for ops on call. Will refine with Inez/Tara tomorrow and then drop a tiny announcement to the company channel.

High level goal:
- Reduce non-essential operational noise while traffic pattern is stable/reduced this weekend.
- Keep customers informed of expected behaviour (short latency blips, background maintenance ability to scale), avoid panic when transient throttles kick in.
- Ensure SRE/Support have crisp responses and escalation paths.

When we flip to quiet-mode:
- Autoscale policy tightened (burst cap retained for paid tiers) — aim: minimize scaling churn overnight.
- Reduce alert sensitivity for low-severity latency jitter for 15m windows (temporary mute threshold). Critical alerts (model OOMs, control-plane auth failures, data-plane 5xx rate >0.5%) remain loud.
- Enable read-only maintenance page for scheduled infra work if we ever cross manual-maintenance threshold.

Why we're doing this (one-liner for execs):
- Short, predictable window to run low-risk infra adjustments and reduce noisy paging during lower traffic; keeps SLO slack for emergency interventions.

Audience segmentation for communications:
- Internal ops/eng (detailed): full checklist, runbook links, oncall names, fallback models.
- Internal company (light): why lower alerts, how to get updates, who to ping if customer impact.
- Customers (if needed): very short status page blurb and scheduled maintenance notice only if we touch public infra.

Draft internal company blurb (short):
Subject: Weekend traffic — temporary "quiet-mode" for ops (Mar 13-15)
Body: Quick heads-up that our infra team will put non-critical alerting and autoscale churn reductions into effect over the weekend to stabilize capacity and run low-risk housekeeping. You should not expect service downtime; any customer-impacting activity will be announced on status.redwood.ai and in #customer-ops. PMs: if you have scheduled demos or high-traffic events, DM me and we’ll set exceptions.

Slack ping templates (short):
- #all: "Ops update: implementing temporary quiet-mode from 22:00 PT Fri to 08:00 PT Mon. No expected downtime. Watch status.redwood.ai for any escalations. Questions ping @MarinAlvarez."
- #eng-all: "FYI: alert sensitivity relaxed for low-severity latency churn this weekend; critical errors still alert. See Confluence: Capacity playbook (link)."

Short on-call crib (for SREs):
- Primary: Inez; backup: Rowan; rotation: standard ring.
- Quick checklist on page load: check status.redwood.ai -> check autoscaling metrics (cluster-cpu, queue-depth) -> check model queue lengths -> look for OOMs/5xx spikes.
- If model-serving latency > 3x baseline for > 10 min AND user impact > 0.2% request errors -> escalate to platform-eng oncall and open JIRA-OPS incident.

Canned support responses (copy/paste friendly):
- "We're in a planned capacity stabilization window. We're not expecting downtime. If you're seeing elevated latency, please share a timestamp and trace id and we will investigate immediately." 
- "Thanks for flagging. This looks like an individual tenant routing delay — we're tracing; we'll follow up in the next 30 minutes."

Three quick risk scenarios & actions:
1) Large capacity dip (node failure cascade): immediate rolling fallback to dedicated-compat model variants; page platform-eng; promote to SEV-1 if customer-facing errors >0.5%.
2) Control-plane auth issues: disable non-critical background jobs, rotate temporary API gateway key if needed, page security lead. Keep customer-notice template ready.
3) Spurious alerts flooding oncall due to telemetry regression: flip mute on the alert group, triage offline, roll back the telemetry change if recent deploy correlates.

Acceptance criteria for flipping quiet-mode back to normal:
- CPU/batch latency back to < 1.25x baseline for 30m.
- No queued requests > normal SLA for 30m.
- No unresolved SEV alerts.

Open questions / TODOs for tomorrow sync with Tara/Inez:
- Exact time window (Fri 22:00 -> Mon 08:00?) confirm with product demo calendar.
- Decide whether to publish a public maintenance banner if we touch control plane signing.
- Finalize the reduced alert thresholds set list and owner for temporary mutes.

Notes to self (raw fragments):
- Keep the company blurb short and reassuring. Avoid promises about "no degradation" — use "not expecting".
- Add a tiny FAQ to Confluence with common Qs and canned answers that Support can copy.
- Run a micro-dry-run with the SRE rotation on Thursday afternoon to ensure everyone knows the mute/unmute flow.
- Consider a short postmortem template ready in case quiet-mode causes user-impact so we don't scramble.

Slack shortcuts/ops snippets (for oncall):
- '/alert mute-group capacity-churn --until 2026-03-15T15:00Z' (example command placeholder)
- 'check-metrics --cluster prod --window 15m --metric queue_depth' (not actual tool, reminder to run equivalent)

My next steps:
- Tweak this doc after Inez's feedback, then publish a 2-line all-hands note Saturday morning if window confirmed.
- Add short FAQ to Confluence and ping support leads to pull in canned responses.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to tidy announcement once collaborators sign off.
